newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal no longer emerging mkt after EDP - official.
newsitem.headline: Portugal no longer emerging mkt after EDP - official.

text.p: Portugal will no longer be considered an emerging market after the privatisation of utility EDP-Electricidade de Portugal this summer, Under-Secretary for Finance Fernando Teixeira dos Santos told a Lisbon newspaper.

"With the entry of EDP to the bourse, the bourse will attain a level of capitalisation and diversification that, in conjunction with Portugal's macroeconomic development programme, will enable the country to leave behind the group of emerging markets," he told Publico.
"The EDP operation will permit the jump from an emerging market to a developed market," he added.
He said he expected strong demand for EDP shares from domestic investors and that the pre-registration period for EDP shares would start on May 19.

"Only after a large part of the pre-registration period is over will the government be able to define the amount of EDP that will be sold off, because we will then have a valuable indicator of the level of demand," he said.
The Socialist government is expected to sell up to 49 percent of EDP in mid-June. EDP will be the largest company quoted on Lisbon bourse.
